card_summary: The NAB Show announcement from SDVI signals a significant shift towards more robust and scalable live signal transport architectures. With the integration of ST 2110 and NMOS, SDVI is poised to further simplify the adoption of IP-based live production, making it easier for engineers to deploy and manage complex signal flows. However, this move also raises concerns about the potential for increased latency, particularly in environments where multiple devices are involved in the signal chain. In practice, this means that engineering teams will need to carefully evaluate their existing infrastructure and signal flow architectures to ensure they can accommodate the increased demands of IP-based live production. The trade-off here is between the benefits of greater scalability and flexibility, and the potential risks of increased latency and signal degradation. To mitigate these risks, engineers should focus on implementing robust genlock and synchronization strategies, such as those enabled by JPEG XS and AES67, to ensure frame-accuracy and signal integrity across the entire signal chain.

Why Broadcasters Must Prioritize Real-Time Transport and Latency in IP Signal Transport

As the industry shifts toward IP-based signal transport, broadcasters are facing a critical inflection point. The pressure to reduce latency, ensure signal integrity, and maintain frame accuracy is mounting. With the increasing adoption of ST 2110 and other IP standards, the stakes are higher than ever. Broadcasters must reassess their infrastructure decisions to ensure they can meet the demands of real-time transport.

What This Development Actually Means

SDVI is set to showcase significant platform enhancements, new technology integrations, and next-generation innovations at the 2026 NAB Show. Specifically, the company will highlight its advancements in IP signal transport, including improved latency and signal integrity. These enhancements are built on top of the ST 2110 standard, which has become the de facto standard for IP-based signal transport in the broadcast industry.

This development is a direct response to the industry's growing demand for lower latency and higher signal integrity. With the increasing adoption of IP-based signal transport, broadcasters are looking for ways to reduce the latency associated with traditional baseband signal transport. SDVI's enhancements address this need, providing a more efficient and reliable way to transport live signals over IP networks.

Why It Matters for Broadcast Operations

For broadcast engineers, this development has significant implications for infrastructure decisions over the next 12-18 months. The integration complexity and CapEx/OpEx trade-offs will be substantial. Broadcasters will need to carefully evaluate the costs and benefits of upgrading their infrastructure to support ST 2110 and other IP standards. In particular, they will need to consider the impact on their existing hardware and software investments, as well as the potential for reduced latency and improved signal integrity.

Real-world vendors like Matrox ConvertIP, Riedel MediorNet, and Pebble Beach Systems will play a crucial role in helping broadcasters navigate this transition. Their products and solutions will need to be compatible with the new IP standards and protocols, ensuring seamless integration with existing infrastructure.

Impact by Stakeholder

  • Regional and national broadcasters: Will need to budget for significant infrastructure upgrades to support ST 2110 and other IP standards. This will involve replacing existing hardware and software with new IP-based solutions, which will require substantial CapEx investments. However, the benefits of reduced latency and improved signal integrity will be substantial, making it a worthwhile investment for broadcasters looking to improve their live signal transport capabilities.
